assumptions.condition: Under policy \(j\in J\) and stratum \(S=s\), the structural action is \(A=A_{c_j(s)}\).
Under policy \(j\in J\) and stratum \(S=s\), the structural outcome is \(Y=Y_{c_j(s)}\).
For every unit and configurations \(c=(r,q)\), \(c'=(r',q')\) in \(\mathcal C\), \(r=Z\) and \(r'\neq Z\) imply \(Y_c\ge Y_{c'}\).
For every unit, \(r=Z\) and \(q\le q'\) imply \(Y_{(r,q)}\le Y_{(r,q')}\).
For every unit, \(r\neq Z\) and \(q\le q'\) imply \(Y_{(r,q)}\ge Y_{(r,q')}\).
\(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with law \(p\in\mathfrak O\).

definitions.name: Selective-Label Counterfactual-Correctness response-type class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}=\{t=(s,z,(a_c),(y_c))\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{raw}}: y_{(z,q)}\ge y_{(1-z,q')}\ \forall q,q'\in\mathcal Q;\ y_{(z,q)}\le y_{(z,q')}\ \forall q\le q';\ y_{(1-z,q)}\ge y_{(1-z,q')}\ \forall q\le q';\ y_{(r_{\mathrm{neu}},q)}=y_{(r_{\mathrm{neu}},q')}\ \forall q,q'\in\mathcal Q\}\).

definitions.name: Finite randomized selective-label SCM class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}=\{M: M\text{ has finite }\mathcal S,J,\mathcal Q,\text{ binary }Z,A,Y,\text{ and satisfies the randomized assignment, known arm-law, common-action, common-outcome, reveal-action, masked-truth, correctness, performance-order, and neutral-invariance conditions}\}\).

definitions.name: Selective-label observable-law map
definitions.construction: For \(o=(j,s,a,y,\ell)\in\mathcal O\) and \(t=(s_t,z_t,(a_c(t)),(y_c(t)))\), set \(B_{o,t}=\rho_j\mathbf 1\{s_t=s,\ a_{c_j(s)}(t)=a,\ y_{c_j(s)}(t)=y,\ \ell=z_t\text{ if }a=1,\ \ell=\star\text{ if }a=0\}\).

definitions.name: Ground-truth-blind comparison programs
definitions.construction: Apply \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}\) to every observable cell and solve the same two programs with \(B_{\mathrm{blind}}=K_{\mathrm{blind}}B\) and right-hand side \(p_{\mathrm{blind}}=K_{\mathrm{blind}}p\).

definitions.name: Finite-sample whole-set confidence construction
definitions.construction: Compute the Bonferroni simultaneous Clopper--Pearson box \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and intersect it with \(\mathfrak O\). When the intersection is nonempty, optimize \(h_e^{\top}v\) over \(v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) subject to \(Bv\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\); when it is empty, return the total fallback interval \([0,1]\).

definitions.name: Euclidean-projection plug-in endpoint estimator
definitions.construction: Project \(\widehat p\) onto \(\mathfrak O\) in Euclidean norm and evaluate both endpoint programs: \(\widehat\theta=\theta(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}\widehat p)\).

definitions.name: Projection-composed endpoint directional map
definitions.construction: First project a direction \(g\) onto \(T_{\mathfrak O}(p)\); then evaluate the support function of the lower optimal dual face and the negative support function of the upper optimal dual face, yielding \(\Gamma'_p(g)\).

definitions.name: Active-cone and dual-face subsampling handle
definitions.construction: Within \(\mathfrak O^{32}\), enumerate boundary faces and retain the smallest face on which projection and both endpoint programs tie. Enumerate its active projection cones and optimal dual faces, compute the exact piecewise-linear Gaussian law of \(\max\{\Gamma'_{p,L}(G_p),-\Gamma'_{p,U}(G_p)\}\), and compare it with the centered without-replacement \(m_n\)-out-of-\(n\) critical value \(c^{\mathrm{sub}}_{n,1-\alpha+\eta_n}\).

definitions.name: Strictly positive four-coordinate witness mixture
definitions.construction: For \(\pi\in\mathcal P_{32}\), set \(\varepsilon_{32}=\pi_4/24\), \(a_{32}=\pi_2-\pi_4/8\), and \(b_{32}=\pi_1+\pi_2-\pi_4/8\). Assign weight \(\varepsilon_{32}\) to every table row except rows \(20\) and \(32\), assign \(a_{32}\) to row \(20\), and assign \(b_{32}\) to row \(32\). The induced full and blind laws are \(B^{32}w^{32}(\pi)\) and \(K^{32}B^{32}w^{32}(\pi)\).

statements.statement: The observable--target image of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) is exactly \(\{(Bw,h_e^{\top}w):w\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}\). In the forward direction, every \(M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) induces its distribution over legal deterministic response types. In the converse direction, every \(w\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) canonically defines an attaining SCM \(M_w\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) by drawing \(t\sim w\), independently drawing \(D\sim\rho\), and reading the structural responses from \(t\).
statements.justification: The converse is the substantive bridge from every feasible latent optimizer to a legally realized human--AI SCM.
statements.gap: DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024, Proposition 1 and Theorem 1, give the general discrete response-function construction; this theorem identifies the exact quotient required by action-dependent truth revelation and the ZhangSkalnesChenOberst2026 common \(q\)-indexed order restrictions.
statements.consumer: It licenses sharp evaluation of an untrialed PSA or assisted-decision policy without treating an algebraic completion as a causal model.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) and define
\[
T=\bigl(S,Z,(A_c)_{c\in\mathcal C},(Y_c)_{c\in\mathcal C}\bigr),\qquad
w_t=\Pr_M(T=t).
\]
The four unit-level restrictions imply the four membership conditions in \(\text{def:legal-response-types}\), so \(T\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\) almost surely.  Thus \(w\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).

Fix \(o=(j,s,a,y,\ell)\in\mathcal O\).  Randomized assignment and the known arm law give \(\Pr(D=j,T=t)=\rho_jw_t\).  Conditional on \(D=j,T=t\), the common-response assumptions give \(A=a_{c_j(s)}(t)\) and \(Y=y_{c_j(s)}(t)\) on \(S=s\).  Revelation and masking give \(\ell=z_t\) when \(a=1\) and \(\ell=\star\) when \(a=0\).  Hence, by the incidence definition,
\[
\Pr_M(O_i=o)
=\sum_t\rho_jw_t\mathbf 1\!\left\{s_t=s,\ a_{c_j(s)}(t)=a,\ y_{c_j(s)}(t)=y,\
\ell=z_t\text{ if }a=1,\ \ell=\star\text{ if }a=0\right\}
=\sum_tB_{o,t}w_t.
\]
Therefore \(p=Bw\).  The target definition gives
\[
\tau_e(M)=\mathbb E_M[Y_{c_e(S)}]
=\sum_tw_ty_{c_e(s_t)}(t)=h_e^{\top}w.
\]

Conversely, fix \(w\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).  Draw \(T=t\) with probability \(w_t\), independently draw \(D=j\) with probability \(\rho_j\), and define \(S,Z,(A_c),(Y_c)\) by the coordinates of \(T\).  Under policy \(j\), set \(A=A_{c_j(S)}\), \(Y=Y_{c_j(S)}\), \(R=A\), and set \(Z_{\mathrm{obs}}=Z\) on \(R=1\) and \(Z_{\mathrm{obs}}=\star\) on \(R=0\).  This construction satisfies randomized assignment, the known arm law, both common-response restrictions, revelation, and masking.  Every supported type is legal, so all four outcome restrictions hold.  Consequently \(M_w\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).  The preceding calculation gives observable law \(Bw\) and target \(h_e^{\top}w\), proving both inclusions.

statements.statement: As a corollary of \(\text{thm:finite-response-converse}\), for every \(p\in\mathfrak O\) the identified set of \(\tau_e\) is \([L(p),U(p)]\); compactness attains both endpoints and mixtures of endpoint SCMs attain every intermediate value.
statements.justification: This corollary records the causal interpretation of the two programs without treating LP compactness as the novelty kernel.
statements.gap: The generic optimization implication is informed by DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024; the application-specific advance is carried by the complete strict-refinement certificate.
statements.consumer: It converts each reported LP interval into the exact set of deployment means compatible with the model.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\in\mathfrak O\) and let
\[
F(p)=\{v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}:Bv=p\}.
\]
This fiber is nonempty, convex, and compact.  By \(\text{thm:finite-response-converse}\), its compatible causal values are exactly
\[
\{\tau_e(M):P_M(O_i)=p,\ M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}
=\{h_e^{\top}v:v\in F(p)\}.
\]
The continuous linear image of a compact convex set in \(\mathbb R\) is a compact interval.  Its attained endpoints are \(L(p)\) and \(U(p)\) by \(\text{def:sharp-endpoint-programs}\).  If \(v_L,v_U\) attain them, then, for \(0\leq\gamma\leq1\),
\[
v_\gamma=(1-\gamma)v_L+\gamma v_U\in F(p),\qquad
h_e^{\top}v_\gamma=(1-\gamma)L(p)+\gamma U(p).
\]
The converse theorem constructs an SCM for every \(v_\gamma\), so the identified set is exactly \([L(p),U(p)]\).

statements.statement: For every \(p\in\mathfrak O\), feasibility under \(Bv=p\) implies feasibility under \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}Bv=K_{\mathrm{blind}}p\), hence \([L(p),U(p)]\subseteq[L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p),U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)]\).
statements.justification: The one-line coarsening fact fixes the direction of comparison used by the strict certificate.
statements.gap: This is a data-processing lemma, not a claim to extend LakkarajuKleinbergLeskovecLudwigMullainathan2017.
statements.consumer: It makes any strict endpoint gap interpretable as information supplied by selectively revealed labels.
statements.proof_tex:
Define
\[
F(p)=\{v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}:Bv=p\},\qquad
F_b(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)
=\{v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}:K_{\mathrm{blind}}Bv=K_{\mathrm{blind}}p\}.
\]
Applying \(K_{\mathrm{blind}}\) to \(Bv=p\) proves \(F(p)\subseteq F_b(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)\).  Minimization over the larger set cannot increase, and maximization cannot decrease.  Therefore
\[
L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p)\leq L(p)\leq U(p)
\leq U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K_{\mathrm{blind}}p),
\]
which is the asserted inclusion.

statements.statement: Under \(\text{def:32-design-specialization}\), all thirty-two rows of \(\text{def:complete-32-type-table}\) are distinct members of \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\). When \(z=0\), the neutral outcomes are constant at one and the \(r=1\) outcomes are nonincreasing; when \(z=1\), the neutral outcomes are constant at zero and the \(r=1\) outcomes are nondecreasing, so correctness, both performance orders, and neutrality hold row by row. The twelve displayed cells are every feasible observable row and each occurs in the table. Every other legal full response type has the same pair \((B_{\cdot,t},h_e(t))\) as one listed row, because its only additional choices are the constant neutral outcome and actions at configurations unused by \(j_{\ell},e_{32},j_h\). Consequently the table generates the full observable polytope and cannot omit a column that changes any of the four optima. For every \(\pi\in\mathcal P_{32}\), the programs formed with \(B^{32}\), \(h^{32}\), and \(K^{32}\) satisfy \(L=\pi_1+\pi_2\), \(U=\pi_1+\pi_2+\pi_4\), \(L_{\mathrm{blind}}=\pi_1\), and \(U_{\mathrm{blind}}=1\). Thus \(p^{32}\) gives \([1/2,3/4]\) versus \([1/4,1]\), while \(p^{32,\circ}\) gives \([397/800,601/800]\) versus \([99/400,1]\). Both laws lie in \(\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O^{32})\), since their displayed mixtures give strictly positive weight to every generator of \(\mathfrak O^{32}=B^{32}\Delta_{31}\).
statements.justification: The full quotient, positive generating mixture, and exact arithmetic establish a legally realized and non-boundary two-sided gain rather than an abstract four-column LP artifact.
statements.gap: ZhangSkalnesChenOberst2026 reports narrower simulated bounds but gives no sharp action-dependent selective-label quotient, exact rational full-versus-blind certificate, or full-polytope relative-interior realization.
statements.consumer: The table is an exact regression fixture for the Imai PSA and aihuman implementations, including every reveal-action pattern and both performance-order directions.
statements.proof_tex:
Use the row order in \(\text{def:complete-32-type-table}\).  For \(z=0\), the neutral outcome triple is constant and the incorrect \(r=1\) triple is one of
\[
000,\quad100,\quad110,\quad111.
\]
The table uses neutral triple \(111\).  Neutral triple \(000\) forces the incorrect triple to be \(000\) and has the same observable column and target as a displayed row.  For \(z=1\), the correct \(r=1\) triple is one of
\[
000,\quad001,\quad011,\quad111.
\]
The table uses neutral triple \(000\); neutral triple \(111\) forces the correct triple to be \(111\) and is again quotient-equivalent to a displayed row.  Thus every displayed outcome array is legal, and every omitted legal outcome array has a displayed representative.

Only \(A_{(1,q_\ell)}\) and \(A_{(1,q_h)}\) enter the trial law, while the target uses only \(Y_{(1,q_m)}\).  Actions at neutral configurations and at \((1,q_m)\) are irrelevant to \((B_{\cdot,t},h_e(t))\).  The four table patterns exhaust \((A_{(1,q_\ell)},A_{(1,q_h)})\in\{0,1\}^2\).  Hence the quotient has \(2\cdot4\cdot4=32\) classes.  The displayed arrays are distinct.  Each arm has two masked \(a=0\) cells and four revealed \(a=1\) cells, and all twelve occur.  The table therefore generates the full observable polytope and omits no column relevant to an endpoint.

For \(\pi_3=\pi_2\), multiplying the mixture by the table gives
\[
\begin{split}
p(\pi)=\bigl(&\pi_4/6,\pi_4/6,\pi_4/24,\pi_2/2+\pi_4/24,\pi_4/8,
\pi_1/2+\pi_2/2-\pi_4/24,\\
&\pi_4/6,\pi_4/6,\pi_4/8,\pi_2/2-\pi_4/24,\pi_4/24,
\pi_1/2+\pi_2/2+\pi_4/24\bigr)^{\top},
\end{split}
\]
and
\[
K^{32}p(\pi)=\bigl(\pi_4/6,\pi_4/6,\pi_2/2+\pi_4/12,
\pi_1/2+\pi_2/2+\pi_4/12,\pi_4/6,\pi_4/6,
\pi_2/2+\pi_4/12,\pi_1/2+\pi_2/2+\pi_4/12\bigr)^{\top}.
\]
In the full and blind row orders define
\[
\lambda_L=(0,0,0,0,0,2,0,0,0,0,2,0)^{\top},
\]
\[
\lambda_U=(0,0,-2,0,0,0,2,2,2,0,2,2)^{\top},
\]
\[
\mu_L=(0,2,0,2,-2,0,-2,0)^{\top},\qquad
\mu_U=(2,2,2,2,0,0,0,0)^{\top}.
\]
The two monotone outcome lists imply, columnwise,
\[
\lambda_L^{\top}B_i\leq h_i\leq\lambda_U^{\top}B_i.
\]
Indeed, the lower expression is the indicator of the low cell \((1,1,1)\) plus that of the high cell \((1,1,0)\).  For \(z=0\), the upper expression is \(1-\mathbf 1\{A_{(1,q_\ell)}=1,Y_{(1,q_\ell)}=0\}\); for \(z=1\), it is \(1-\mathbf 1\{A_{(1,q_h)}=1,Y_{(1,q_h)}=0\}\).  Similarly,
\[
\mu_L^{\top}K^{32}B_i
=Y_{(1,q_\ell)}+Y_{(1,q_h)}-1\leq h_i,\qquad
h_i\leq1=\mu_U^{\top}K^{32}B_i.
\]
Thus weak duality and the displayed laws give
\[
L\geq\pi_1+\pi_2,\quad U\leq\pi_1+\pi_2+\pi_4,\quad
L_{\mathrm{blind}}\geq\pi_1,\quad U_{\mathrm{blind}}\leq1.
\]

Here are attaining primal certificates.  Notation \(\{i:x,\ldots\}\) gives the nonzero coordinates.  Put \(r_1=(1,0,0)\), \(r_2=(0,1,0)\), and \(r_3=(0,1,8)\) in \((\pi_1,\pi_2,\pi_4)\)-coordinates:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|l}
X&v_1^X&v_2^X&v_3^X\\\hline
FL&\{32:1\}&\{20:1,32:1\}&
\{3:2/3,6:2,7:2,14:2/3,18:1/3,21:2/3,22:5/3,23:5/3,31:1/3\}\\
FU&\{32:1\}&\{20:1,32:1\}&
\{3:2/3,10:2,11:2,14:2/3,18:1/3,25:2/3,26:5/3,27:5/3,31:1/3\}\\
BL&\{32:1\}&\{8:1,24:1\}&
\{5:8/3,8:7/3,21:8/3,24:7/3\}\\
BU&\{32:1\}&\{12:1,28:1\}&
\{9:8/3,12:7/3,25:8/3,28:7/3\}.
\end{array}
\]
Direct addition of the two half-incidence entries of every listed column verifies
\[
B^{32}v_k^{FL}=B^{32}v_k^{FU}=p(r_k),\qquad
K^{32}B^{32}v_k^{BL}=K^{32}B^{32}v_k^{BU}=K^{32}p(r_k).
\]
The masses for \(k=1,2,3\) are \(1,2,10\).  Their target sums are
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
X&h^{\top}v_1^X&h^{\top}v_2^X&h^{\top}v_3^X\\\hline
FL&1&1&1\\ FU&1&1&9\\ BL&1&0&0\\ BU&1&2&10.
\end{array}
\]
For \(\pi\in\mathcal P_{32}\), set
\[
v^X(\pi)=\pi_1v_1^X+\left(\pi_2-\frac{\pi_4}{8}\right)v_2^X
+\frac{\pi_4}{8}v_3^X.
\]
The coefficients are nonnegative, and the total mass is
\[
\pi_1+2(\pi_2-\pi_4/8)+10\pi_4/8=\pi_1+2\pi_2+\pi_4=1.
\]
Linearity and \(\pi=\pi_1r_1+(\pi_2-\pi_4/8)r_2+(\pi_4/8)r_3\) show feasibility.  The target table gives the four reverse inequalities, proving
\[
L=\pi_1+\pi_2,\quad U=\pi_1+\pi_2+\pi_4,\quad
L_{\mathrm{blind}}=\pi_1,\quad U_{\mathrm{blind}}=1.
\]
Substitution gives \([1/2,3/4]\) versus \([1/4,1]\) at \(\pi^{32}\), and \([397/800,601/800]\) versus \([99/400,1]\) at \(\pi^{32,\circ}\); the formula for \(p(\pi)\) gives the two stated rational laws.

Finally, \(\varepsilon_{32}=\pi_4/24>0\), \(a_{32}=\pi_2-\pi_4/8>0\), and \(b_{32}=\pi_1+a_{32}>0\).  Thus every generator has positive weight.  A positive combination of every point in a finite convex hull lies in its relative interior: any nonnegative affine supporting functional vanishing at that combination must vanish at every generator.  Applying this fact proves that both witness laws lie in \(\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O^{32})\).

statements.statement: There is a nonempty relatively open set \(\mathcal U\subset\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O^{32})\) containing \(p^{32,\circ}\) such that \(L(p)>L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K^{32}p)\) and \(U(p)<U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K^{32}p)\) for every \(p\in\mathcal U\). The conclusion follows from the two strict gaps \(199/800\) at \(p^{32,\circ}\) and continuity of the four finite-polyhedral value functions on relative interior.
statements.justification: The relative-open theorem is the field-level kernel: selectively revealed truth improves both endpoints throughout a stable region of the actual full model.
statements.gap: Neither ZhangSkalnesChenOberst2026 nor BenMichaelGreinerHuangImaiJiangShin2025 establishes a legally realized, relatively open, two-sided information gain under these response restrictions.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts obtain a stable diagnostic for when selectively collected outcomes materially improve both deployment bounds.
statements.proof_tex:
At \(p_0=p^{32,\circ}\), the certificate gives
\[
L(p_0)-L_{\mathrm{blind}}(K^{32}p_0)=199/800,\qquad
U_{\mathrm{blind}}(K^{32}p_0)-U(p_0)=199/800.
\]
The lower value is convex and the upper value is concave on the observable polytope: convex combinations of feasible weights prove the two inequalities.  Both are bounded in \([0,1]\).

We prove the needed relative-interior continuity.  Let \(f:C\to[0,1]\) be convex and \(x_0\in\operatorname{relint}(C)\).  Choose \(r>0\) such that the relative radius-\(r\) ball about \(x_0\) lies in \(C\).  For \(x=x_0+du\), \(0<d<r\), \(\|u\|_2=1\),
\[
x=(1-d/r)x_0+(d/r)(x_0+ru)
\]
gives \(f(x)\leq f(x_0)+d/r\), while
\[
x_0=\frac r{r+d}x+\frac d{r+d}(x_0-ru)
\]
gives \(f(x)\geq f(x_0)-d/r\).  Hence \(f\) is continuous at \(x_0\); applying this to \(-f\) proves the concave case.

The certificate puts \(p_0\) in \(\operatorname{relint}(\mathfrak O^{32})\).  Its positive generator representation also puts \(K^{32}p_0\) in the relative interior of the blind image.  Hence all four value functions, with the blind pair composed with \(K^{32}\), are continuous at \(p_0\).  The two positive gaps remain positive on a relatively open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\) of \(p_0\), proving the claim.

statements.statement: Applying the generic simultaneous-region propagation of DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024, Section 6 and Appendix E, to the SLCC incidence program gives \(\Pr_p\{[L(p),U(p)]\subseteq\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(n\ge1\) and \(p\in\mathfrak O\). On \(p\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\), the intersection \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathfrak O\) is nonempty and the implementation optima are attained.
statements.justification: This implementation corollary supplies an exact conservative reporting procedure while acknowledging the generic propagation theorem as prior art.
statements.gap: DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024, Section 6 and Appendix E, already establish generic confidence-region propagation; the contribution here is its explicit implementation for the SLCC incidence map, not a new inference principle.
statements.consumer: The aihuman analysis can report a finite-sample envelope for the entire sharp PSA deployment interval.
statements.proof_tex:
For each \(o\), \(N_o\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,p_o)\).  Exact Clopper--Pearson coverage and the union bound give
\[
\Pr_p\{p\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\}
\geq1-\sum_{o\in\mathcal O}\frac{\alpha}{|\mathcal O|}=1-\alpha.
\]
On this event, \(p\in\mathfrak O\cap\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\).  Every \(v\) with \(Bv=p\) is feasible for the confidence optimization, so sharpness gives
\[
[L(p),U(p)]
=\{h_e^{\top}v:Bv=p,\ v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}
\subseteq
\{h_e^{\top}v:Bv\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha},\ v\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}
=\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}.
\]
Thus the asserted coverage is at least \(1-\alpha\).  Off this event an empty intersection triggers \([0,1]\), which still contains the identified set.  When the intersection is nonempty, its feasible weights form a nonempty closed subset of the compact simplex; their linear image is a compact interval and both implementation optima are attained.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(p\in\mathfrak O\), the map \(x\mapsto\theta(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}x)\) is Hadamard directionally differentiable at \(p\) with derivative \(\Gamma'_p\), and \(\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta-\theta(p)\}\rightsquigarrow\Gamma'_p(G_p)\). This formula remains valid when \(p\) is on a projection face and either endpoint has multiple optimal bases.
statements.justification: The limit law exposes both sources of nonregularity instead of imposing margin conditions that remove simultaneous ties.
statements.gap: FangSantos2019, Theorem 2.1 and Section 4, supplies the directional delta method and projection derivative; ZhangSkalnesChenOberst2026, Theorem 5.1, assumes margin separation. The new formula composes the observable-polytope projection with both LP optimal-face maps for this causal identified set.
statements.consumer: It supplies pointwise standard-error simulation and diagnoses exactly when ordinary Gaussian endpoint intervals fail in finite human--AI trials.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\Phi(x)=\theta(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}x)\).  For \(x_k=p+t_kg_k\), \(t_k\downarrow0\), \(g_k\to g\), put \(q_k=\Pi_{\mathfrak O}x_k\) and \(d_k=(q_k-p)/t_k\).  Projection against feasible \(p\) gives \(\|q_k-x_k\|_2\leq t_k\|g_k\|_2\), so \((d_k)\) is bounded.  The projection variational inequality is
\[
\langle x_k-q_k,v-q_k\rangle\leq0\qquad(v\in\mathfrak O).
\]
Every subsequential limit \(d\) lies in \(T_{\mathfrak O}(p)\).  For a radial \(z\), substitute \(v=p+t_kz\), divide by \(t_k^2\), and pass to the limit.  Closure then gives
\[
\langle g-d,z-d\rangle\leq0\qquad(z\in T_{\mathfrak O}(p)).
\]
This uniquely characterizes \(d=\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g\).  Hence the projection is Hadamard directionally differentiable with that derivative, including at a proper face.

Now consider
\[
\mathcal P=\operatorname{conv}\{(B_{\cdot,t},h_e(t)):t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\}.
\]
Its lower and upper boundary functions are \(L\) and \(U\).  Its finitely many supporting facets show locally that \(L\) is a maximum of finitely many affine lower supports and \(U\) is a minimum of finitely many affine upper supports.  Their active slopes are precisely the normalized dual faces \(\Lambda_L(p)\) and \(\Lambda_U(p)\).  Therefore, for \(r_k=p+t_kz_k\in\mathfrak O\), \(z_k\to z\),
\[
\frac{L(r_k)-L(p)}{t_k}\to\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda_L(p)}\lambda^{\top}z,\qquad
\frac{U(r_k)-U(p)}{t_k}\to\min_{\lambda\in\Lambda_U(p)}\lambda^{\top}z.
\]
Inactive facets have a strict gap and disappear for large \(k\); this proves the formula without a unique basis.  Composing with the projection derivative yields
\[
\Phi'_p(g)=
\left(
\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda_L(p)}\lambda^{\top}\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g,\
\min_{\lambda\in\Lambda_U(p)}\lambda^{\top}\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O}(p)}g
\right)=\Gamma'_p(g).
\]
This is a continuous finite piecewise-linear map.  By \(\text{lem:finite-multinomial-clt}\),
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat p-p)\rightsquigarrow G_p.
\]
Applying \(\text{lem:hadamard-directional-delta-method}\) gives
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat\theta-\theta(p)\}\rightsquigarrow\Gamma'_p(G_p).
\]
The derivation allowed a projection face and retained the entire optimal dual faces, proving the final assertion.

statements.statement: If there is \(j^{\star}\in J_0\) with \(c_e(s)=c_{j^{\star}}(s)\) for every \(s\in\mathcal S\), then \(L(p)=U(p)=\mathbb E[Y\mid D=j^{\star}]\). Separately, if \(A_c=1\) for every \(c\in\mathcal C\), then \(Z\) is fully observed, but full revelation alone does not point-identify every distinct untrialed configuration: there exist two legal SCMs with the same fully labeled trial law and different untrialed means. Identification may nevertheless occur at special observed laws, through configuration overlap, through the neutral-invariance restriction, or under further identifying restrictions.
statements.justification: The sanity check recovers ordinary randomized identification exactly under configuration equality and keeps full revelation logically separate from policy overlap.
statements.gap: ImaiJiangGreinerHalenShin2023 identifies observed randomized recommendation arms; the reduction embeds precisely that case and makes no universal identification claim for a distinct untrialed configuration.
statements.consumer: Implementations can test the standard RCT case without falsely declaring identification merely because all labels are revealed.
statements.proof_tex:
If \(c_e(s)=c_{j^\star}(s)\) for every \(s\), then \(h_e(t)=y_{c_{j^\star}(s_t)}(t)\).  Since \(\rho_{j^\star}>0\), randomization and the common outcome response give, for every compatible \(v\),
\[
\mathbb E_v[Y\mid D=j^\star]
=\rho_{j^\star}^{-1}\sum_tv_t\rho_{j^\star}y_{c_{j^\star}(s_t)}(t)
=h_e^{\top}v.
\]
The left side is fixed by \(p\), so every \(v\) in the fiber has that target.  Sharpness gives \(L(p)=U(p)=\mathbb E[Y\mid D=j^\star]\).

If \(A_c=1\) for every \(c\), then \(R=1\) and \(Z_{\mathrm{obs}}=Z\) almost surely.  Nevertheless full revelation alone need not identify a distinct configuration.  Take one stratum, a trialed configuration \((1,q_\ell)\), an untrialed configuration \((1,q_h)\), and \(q_\ell<q_h\).  In two deterministic SCMs set \(Z=1\), all actions to one, and all neutral outcomes to zero.  Set
\[
(Y_{(1,q_\ell)},Y_{(1,q_h)})=(0,0)
\quad\text{in the first model},\qquad
(Y_{(1,q_\ell)},Y_{(1,q_h)})=(0,1)
\quad\text{in the second}.
\]
Both types satisfy correctness, neutrality, and both performance orders.  Their fully labeled trial laws coincide, but their untrialed means are zero and one.  This proves that revelation alone is insufficient while leaving intact the stated special-law, overlap, neutral-invariance, and further-restriction exceptions.

statements.statement:
Fix \(p\in\mathfrak O\), put \(\beta=1-\alpha\), write \((D_L,D_U)=\Gamma'_p\), and define \(H(g)=\max\{D_L(g),-D_U(g)\}\).  Let
\[
V_p=\{g:\mathbf 1^{\top}g=0,\ g_o=0\text{ whenever }p_o=0\}.
\]
Suppose the active projection cones and extreme slopes of \(\Lambda_L(p)\) and \(\Lambda_U(p)\), refined by their zero and comparison hyperplanes, yield a finite polyhedral fan on \(V_p\) such that: (i) locally,
\[
\theta(\Pi_{\mathfrak O}(p+x))-\theta(p)=(D_L(x),D_U(x)),
\]
with both coordinates linear on each fan cone; (ii) every facet normal is nonzero on \(V_p\); and (iii) on every full-dimensional cone where \(H\equiv0\), either the slope of \(D_L\) is zero and \(-D_U\leq0\), or the slope of \(D_U\) is zero and \(D_L\leq0\).  Let \(\mathcal A_p\) be the finite closure under row selection and sign changes of matrices whose nonzero rows are the fan facet normals and nonzero endpoint slopes.  For
\[
X_m=m^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^m(e_{O_i}-p),
\]
from an independent size-\(m\) categorical sample, define
\[
\delta_m(p)=\max_{A\in\mathcal A_p}\sup_x
\left|\Pr_p\{AX_m\leq x\}-\Pr\{AG_p\leq x\}\right|.
\]
Assume \(G_p\) is nondegenerate on \(V_p\),
\[
m_n\to\infty,\qquad m_n^2/n\to0,\qquad\eta_n\downarrow0,
\]
and
\[
\frac{\delta_{m_n}(p)+m_n/\sqrt n+m_n^2/n}{\eta_n}\to0.
\]
Then \(\delta_m(p)\to0\), atoms of \(H(G_p)\) can occur only at zero, and
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr_p\left\{
L(p)\geq\widehat L-\frac{c^{\mathrm{sub}}_{n,1-\alpha+\eta_n}}{\sqrt n},\
U(p)\leq\widehat U+\frac{c^{\mathrm{sub}}_{n,1-\alpha+\eta_n}}{\sqrt n}
\right\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]
No projection-cone or LP-basis uniqueness is required.  The fan, the exact multinomial probabilities defining \(\delta_m(p)\), and the Gaussian orthant probabilities are finite and enumerable.

For the thirty-two-type table the conditions are nonvacuous.  In its stated row order, let
\[
p_\star=B^{32}_{\cdot,1}=B^{32}_{\cdot,17}
=\tfrac12(\mathbf e_1+\mathbf e_7).
\]
This is a boundary vertex of \(\mathfrak O^{32}\), and every mixture of types \(1\) and \(17\) is optimal for both endpoint programs.  If \(\zeta\sim\mathcal N(0,1/4)\), then \(G_{p_\star}=\zeta(\mathbf e_1-\mathbf e_7)\), and exact active-cone enumeration gives
\[
D_L(G_{p_\star})=0,\qquad
D_U(G_{p_\star})=\frac45|\zeta|,\qquad
H(G_{p_\star})=0.
\]
Thus the exact Gaussian directional law is the unit atom at zero, and the asserted conservative conclusion holds for every \(m_n\to\infty\) with \(m_n^2/n\to0\) and every decreasing slack dominating the displayed computable error rate.
statements.justification: Finite active-cone geometry and a slack-dominating multinomial approximation rate make centered subsampling conservative even at the only possible atom, zero.
statements.gap: FangSantos2019 supplies the directional delta method but not atom-valid centered subsampling; the result gives a finite, enumerable certificate specialized to the projection-composed pair of endpoint programs.
statements.consumer: The boundary implementation can certify whether a chosen subsample and slack schedule supports simultaneous endpoint reporting without imposing unique LP bases.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(d=|\mathcal O|\), let \(\Phi=\theta\circ\Pi_{\mathfrak O}\), and put
\[
X_n=\sqrt n(\widehat p-p),\qquad
T_n=\max\{\sqrt n(\widehat L-L(p)),\sqrt n(U(p)-\widehat U)\}.
\]
By \(\text{lem:finite-multinomial-clt}\), using \(\text{ass:iid-finite-sampling}\),
\[
X_n\rightsquigarrow G_p
\quad\text{and hence}\quad X_n=O_p(1).
\tag{1}
\]
The support restrictions in the definition of \(V_p\) hold almost surely for \(X_n\): its coordinates sum to zero, and if \(p_o=0\), then no observation occupies cell \(o\).  By condition (i), there is \(r>0\) such that
\[
\Phi(p+x)-\Phi(p)=(D_L(x),D_U(x))
\quad\text{for every }x\in V_p\text{ with }\|x\|_2<r.
\tag{2}
\]
Both directional coordinates are continuous, positively homogeneous, piecewise-linear functions on the finite fan.  Therefore there is a finite constant \(C_D\) such that
\[
|D_L(x)|\vee |D_U(x)|\leq C_D\|x\|_2,
\qquad x\in V_p.
\tag{3}
\]
Equations (1)--(2) give
\[
T_n=H(X_n)
\tag{4}
\]
with probability tending to one.  Since \(H\) is continuous, every bounded continuous test function \(f\) gives another bounded continuous function \(f\circ H\); the definition of weak convergence in (1) therefore gives \(H(X_n)\rightsquigarrow H(G_p)\).

We next establish the approximation that will be used for the conditional subsampling law.  Write \(m=m_n\), let \(\widehat p_b\) be the empirical law in a uniformly sampled size-\(m\) subsample without replacement, and define
\[
a_n=\sqrt m(\widehat p-p)=\sqrt{m/n}\,X_n.
\tag{5}
\]
Whenever \(\widehat p\) and \(\widehat p_b\) are in the neighborhood in (2), the centered subsample statistic is
\[
S_{n,b}
=\max\{D_L(\sqrt m(\widehat p_b-p))-D_L(a_n),
D_U(a_n)-D_U(\sqrt m(\widehat p_b-p))\}.
\tag{6}
\]
To compare (6) with an independent experiment, first couple the ordered sample of indices without replacement to \(m\) indices sampled with replacement from \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).  The two samples agree unless a repeated index occurs, so, conditionally on the data, the failure probability is at most
\[
\frac{m(m-1)}{2n}.
\tag{7}
\]
Next couple one draw from the empirical categorical law \(\widehat p\) to one draw from \(p\) by assigning matching category \(o\) probability \(\min\{\widehat p_o,p_o\}\) and distributing the two residual masses over the unmatched categories.  Its mismatch probability is \(1-\sum_o\min\{\widehat p_o,p_o\}=\operatorname{TV}(\widehat p,p)\).  Applying this construction independently to the \(m\) draws and using the union bound, all categories agree except on an event of conditional probability at most
\[
m\,\operatorname{TV}(\widehat p,p)
=\frac m2\|\widehat p-p\|_1
=O_p(m/\sqrt n),
\tag{8}
\]
where the final equality follows from (1) and finiteness of \(d\).  On the successful coupling event,
\[
\sqrt m(\widehat p_b-p)=X_m
\]
for the independent-
\(p\) vector in the statement.  Thus the comparison variable is
\[
K_{a_n}(X_m)
=\max\{D_L(X_m)-D_L(a_n),D_U(a_n)-D_U(X_m)\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Notice that the population centering in (9), rather than a translation inside \(D_L\) or \(D_U\), is forced by the identity \(\sqrt m(\widehat p_b-p)=\sqrt m(\widehat p_b-\widehat p)+a_n\).

The exceptional event on which (2) cannot be used has probability tending to zero.  More precisely, boundedness and centering of each categorical summand give \(\mathbb E\exp\{u(e_{O_i,o}-p_o)\}\leq\exp(Cu^2)\) for all sufficiently small \(|u|\), by the power-series bound \(e^v\leq1+v+C'v^2\) on a bounded interval.  Independence, exponential Markov inequality, and a union bound over the finite coordinates then give an exponential bound \(C_0e^{-c_0m}\) for the independent-
\(p\) event \(\|X_m\|_2>r\sqrt m/2\), while (1) and (5) put \(\widehat p\) in the radius-
\(r/2\) neighborhood with probability tending to one.  This exponential term is harmless in the sole case below where an \(o(\eta_n)\) comparison is needed.  Indeed, if \(F(0-)=\beta>0\), then \(H(G_p)<0\) with positive probability, so at least one nonzero endpoint slope belongs to \(\mathcal A_p\).  The law of its value on \(X_m\) is discrete with at most \((m+1)^d\) support points and hence has an atom of size at least \((m+1)^{-d}\).  Its Gaussian counterpart is continuous by nondegeneracy.  Comparing the distribution functions immediately before and at that atom yields
\[
\delta_m(p)\geq\frac{1}{2(m+1)^d}.
\tag{10}
\]
Consequently \(e^{-c_0m}=o(\delta_m(p))\).  If \(F(0-)<\beta\), only convergence of the exceptional probability to zero is needed because there is a fixed probability gap.

We now verify that \(\delta_m(p)\to0\), rather than treating it as an additional assumption.  Equation (1), with \(n\) replaced by \(m\), implies
\[
AX_m\rightsquigarrow AG_p
\tag{11}
\]
for every \(A\in\mathcal A_p\): for each bounded continuous \(f\), the function \(x\mapsto f(Ax)\) is bounded and continuous in the defining convergence (1).  Delete any identically zero rows of \(A\).  Every remaining row is nonzero on \(V_p\), by condition (ii) and the construction of \(\mathcal A_p\), and therefore has strictly positive Gaussian variance because \(G_p\) is nondegenerate on \(V_p\).  Hence every marginal of \(AG_p\) is continuous.  Its joint distribution function is continuous as well, because the probability of the boundary of any lower orthant is bounded by the sum of the point probabilities of its marginals.  A finite grid on a sufficiently large compact box, monotonicity of distribution functions between grid points, and tightness outside the box upgrade the pointwise convergence from (11) to uniform convergence over lower orthants.  Since \(\mathcal A_p\) is finite,
\[
\delta_m(p)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{12}
\]

The events obtained by selecting a fan cone and comparing the two affine expressions in (9) are finite Boolean combinations of half-spaces whose normals are rows of matrices in \(\mathcal A_p\).  Closure of \(\mathcal A_p\) under row selection and sign changes, inclusion--exclusion, (3), and (12) therefore show that, conditionally on the data,
\[
S_{n,b}\rightsquigarrow H(G_p)
\quad\text{in probability}.
\tag{13}
\]
For clarity, the quantitative error in this comparison on \(\{\|X_n\|_2\leq M\}\), at every continuity point of the limiting distribution, is bounded by a constant depending only on the fixed fan and \(M\) times
\[
R_n:=\delta_m(p)+\frac m{\sqrt n}+\frac{m^2}{n}.
\tag{14}
\]
Indeed, (7)--(8) give the last two terms; (5) and (3) move each nonzero Gaussian linear threshold by at most \(C M\sqrt{m/n}\leq C M m/\sqrt n\); and a nonzero Gaussian linear functional has a bounded density, so every resulting Gaussian slab has probability at most another constant times its width.  The same half-space comparison with threshold zero will be used below.

Let \(F(x)=\Pr\{H(G_p)\leq x\}\).  On each full-dimensional cone of the refined fan, the comparison hyperplanes select one of the two endpoint slopes, so \(H\) is a single linear functional there.  Proper fan boundaries have Gaussian probability zero by condition (ii) and nondegeneracy.  A nonzero linear functional of \(G_p\) has a continuous distribution, while a zero linear functional equals zero.  Positive homogeneity also rules out a nonzero constant linear piece.  It follows that
\[
F\text{ can have an atom only at }0.
\tag{15}
\]

Let \(c_n=c^{\mathrm{sub}}_{n,\beta+\eta_n}\) and \(q_\beta=\inf\{x:F(x)\geq\beta\}\).  Suppose first that \(q_\beta\neq0\).  For every sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), the point \(x_\varepsilon=q_\beta-\varepsilon\) is nonzero and satisfies \(F(x_\varepsilon)<\beta\).  By (13), the conditional probability \(\Pr^*\{S_{n,b}\leq x_\varepsilon\}\) is below \(\beta+\eta_n\) with probability tending to one, and hence \(c_n>x_\varepsilon\) with probability tending to one.  The indicator of \(( -\infty,x_\varepsilon]\) can be squeezed from above and below by bounded continuous functions whose limiting expectations differ by arbitrarily little, because (15) gives \(\Pr\{H(G_p)=x_\varepsilon\}=0\).  Applying this squeeze to the weak convergence following (4) gives
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr\{T_n\leq c_n\}
\geq F(x_\varepsilon).
\]
Letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) and using continuity of \(F\) at the nonzero point \(q_\beta\) yields
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr\{T_n\leq c_n\}\geq F(q_\beta)\geq\beta.
\tag{16}
\]

It remains to handle \(q_\beta=0\), where
\[
F(0-)\leq\beta\leq F(0).
\tag{17}
\]
Fix a realization \(z=X_n\) satisfying \(H(z)=0\).  Since a maximum is zero only if both its arguments are nonpositive, positive homogeneity and (5) give
\[
D_L(a_n)=\sqrt{m/n}\,D_L(z)\leq0,
\qquad
D_U(a_n)=\sqrt{m/n}\,D_U(z)\geq0.
\tag{18}
\]
If \(g\) lies in the interior of a full-dimensional cone on which \(H\equiv0\), condition (iii) makes (9) nonnegative.  Indeed, when the lower slope vanishes,
\[
D_L(g)-D_L(a_n)=-D_L(a_n)\geq0,
\]
and when the upper slope vanishes,
\[
D_U(a_n)-D_U(g)=D_U(a_n)\geq0.
\]
In fact, (18) gives the global sign implication
\[
K_{a_n}(g)<0
\ \Longrightarrow\ D_L(g)<D_L(a_n)\leq0
\text{ and }D_U(g)>D_U(a_n)\geq0
\ \Longrightarrow\ H(g)<0.
\tag{19a}
\]
Thus the zero-flatness condition supplies an enumerable cone-wise certificate for the sign preservation, while (19a) shows that proper fan boundaries cannot create an unaccounted negative centered value.  The half-space comparison underlying (14), together with (18)--(19a), therefore gives, uniformly on \(\{\|X_n\|_2\leq M,H(X_n)=0\}\),
\[
\Pr^*\{S_{n,b}<0\}
\leq F(0-)+C_M R_n+r_{n,M},
\tag{19}
\]
where \(r_{n,M}=o(\eta_n)\) if \(F(0-)=\beta\), by (10), and \(r_{n,M}=o(1)\) if \(F(0-)<\beta\).  Thus (10) absorbs the local-neighborhood exception when equality holds in the left inequality of (17), while the fixed probability gap absorbs it otherwise.  By the assumed slack domination, \(R_n/\eta_n\to0\).  The conditional subsampling distribution has finite support, and its lower \((\beta+\eta_n)\)-quantile is nonnegative whenever its mass strictly below zero is smaller than \(\beta+\eta_n\).  Since \(X_n=O_p(1)\), (17)--(19) therefore imply
\[
\Pr\{H(X_n)=0,\ c_n<0\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{20}
\]

We also have \(c_n=o_p(1)\).  For each \(\varepsilon>0\), the definition \(q_\beta=0\) gives \(F(-\varepsilon)<\beta\), so (13) implies \(c_n> -\varepsilon\) with probability tending to one.  Moreover \(F(\varepsilon)>\beta\).  This is immediate if \(F(0)>\beta\).  If \(F(0)=\beta\) and \(H\) takes a positive value, continuity and positive homogeneity give an open Gaussian-positive set on which \(0<H\leq\varepsilon\); if \(H\) never takes a positive value, then \(F(\varepsilon)=1>\beta\).  Applying (13) again yields \(c_n\leq\varepsilon\) with probability tending to one.  Hence
\[
c_n=o_p(1).
\tag{21}
\]

The zero set of \(H\) is a union of full-dimensional zero-cone interiors and subsets of finitely many proper fan hyperplanes.  Its boundary is therefore Gaussian-null.  Continuous functions that equal one away from an arbitrarily small neighborhood of this boundary and zero on the opposite side squeeze the indicator of the zero set; applying (1) to those functions gives
\[
\Pr\{H(X_n)=0\}\longrightarrow F(0)-F(0-).
\tag{22}
\]
For any \(\varepsilon>0\), (20)--(21) cover, with probability tending to one, both observations for which \(H(X_n)\leq-\varepsilon\) and observations for which \(H(X_n)=0\).  Using (4), (15), and (22),
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr\{T_n\leq c_n\}
\geq F(-\varepsilon)+F(0)-F(0-).
\]
Letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) makes the right-hand side \(F(0)\), which is at least \(\beta\) by (17).  Together with (16), this proves
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr\{T_n\leq c_n\}\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{23}
\]
By the definition of \(T_n\), the event in (23) is exactly
\[
\left\{L(p)\geq\widehat L-c_n/\sqrt n,\quad
U(p)\leq\widehat U+c_n/\sqrt n\right\},
\]
which proves the asserted simultaneous endpoint coverage.

It remains to verify the promised boundary certificate.  By \(\text{thm:complete-32-type-refinement-certificate}\), the table contains the full observable--target quotient.  Every column of \(B^{32}\) is nonnegative and has one entry \(1/2\) in each trial-arm block.  If a convex combination of columns equals
\[
p_\star=\tfrac12(\mathbf e_1+\mathbf e_7),
\]
then every positively weighted column must be supported on rows \(1\) and \(7\).  Inspection of \(\text{def:complete-32-type-table}\) shows that precisely columns \(1\) and \(17\) have this support, that they coincide, and that \(h^{32}_1=h^{32}_{17}=0\).  Thus \(p_\star\) is a vertex, its fiber is the segment joining types \(1\) and \(17\), and every point of that segment is optimal for both endpoint programs with value zero.  The multinomial covariance on the two positive cells gives
\[
G_{p_\star}=\zeta(\mathbf e_1-\mathbf e_7),
\qquad \zeta\sim\mathcal N(0,1/4).
\tag{24}
\]

For \(\zeta>0\), the table supplies four high-arm outgoing cells, rows \(8,9,10,12\), while retaining row \(1\) in the low arm.  We first verify that using the remaining high-arm cell, row \(11\), cannot improve the projection.  Divide all candidate tangent coordinates by \(\zeta\), let \(t\geq0\) be the coordinate of row \(11\), and let \(r\geq0\) be the sum of the other four high-arm outgoing coordinates.  Every table column entering row \(11\) also enters low-arm row \(2\) or row \(5\).  Thus the low-arm outgoing mass is at least \(t\), and its squared-distance contribution is at least \((1+t)^2+t^2/2\).  For fixed \((r,t)\), equal allocation among the other four high-arm cells minimizes their sum of squares, so the high-arm contribution is at least \((1-r-t)^2+r^2/4+t^2\).  The sum
\[
(1+t)^2+\frac{t^2}{2}+(1-r-t)^2+\frac{r^2}{4}+t^2
\]
is convex on \(r,t\geq0\); its derivative in \(t\) is \(2r+7t\), and its minimum is therefore at \(t=0\), followed by \(r=4/5\).  Hence the low-arm block is fixed at the projection, and if the four accessible outgoing masses are \(x_1,\ldots,x_4\), with \(s=\sum_{k=1}^4x_k\), the squared Euclidean distance, after division by \(\zeta^2\), is
\[
1+(1-s)^2+\sum_{k=1}^4x_k^2.
\]
For a fixed \(s\), the sum of squares is minimized at \(x_k=s/4\); minimizing \((1-s)^2+s^2/4\) gives \(s=4/5\) and \(x_k=1/5\).  Hence
\[
\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O^{32}}(p_\star)}
\{\zeta(\mathbf e_1-\mathbf e_7)\}
=\frac{\zeta}{5}(-4\mathbf e_7+mathbf e_8+mathbf e_9+mathbf e_{10}+mathbf e_{12}).
\tag{25}
\]
For \(\zeta<0\), the arm-swapped calculation uses low-arm outgoing rows \(2,3,4,5\) and yields
\[
\Pi_{T_{\mathfrak O^{32}}(p_\star)}
\{\zeta(\mathbf e_1-\mathbf e_7)\}
=\frac{|\zeta|}{5}(-4\mathbf e_1+mathbf e_2+mathbf e_3+mathbf e_4+mathbf e_5).
\tag{26}
\]
All four outgoing cells in either (25) or (26) have target-zero representatives in the complete table, and all targets are nonnegative.  Therefore the lower directional value is
\[
D_L(G_{p_\star})=0.
\tag{27}
\]
Exactly two of the four outgoing cells on either ray also have target-one representatives.  Because an incidence entry equals \(1/2\), producing probability \(|\zeta|/5\) in either such cell requires type-weight derivative \(2|\zeta|/5\).  Assigning both cells to their target-one representatives attains target derivative \(4|\zeta|/5\).  The exhaustive table shows that the other two outgoing cells have no target-one representative, so this value is also an upper bound.  Consequently
\[
D_U(G_{p_\star})=\frac45|\zeta|,
\qquad H(G_{p_\star})=0.
\tag{28}
\]
Because \(\mathfrak O^{32}\) is a polytope, a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(p_\star\) agrees with the corresponding neighborhood of \(p_\star+T_{\mathfrak O^{32}}(p_\star)\).  If \(y=\Pi_{\mathfrak O^{32}}(p_\star+x)\), projection optimality with the feasible point \(p_\star\) gives \(\|y-p_\star\|_2^2\leq x^{\top}(y-p_\star)\), and hence \(\|y-p_\star\|_2\leq\|x\|_2\).  Therefore sufficiently small inputs project inside that common neighborhood, and (25)--(26) are exact local projection formulas, not merely first-order approximations.  The exhaustive target-zero and target-one allocations used in (27)--(28) remain feasible with weights linear in \(|\zeta|\) for all sufficiently small \(|\zeta|\), and their matching upper bounds are linear as well.  Thus the endpoint formulas are locally exact.  The two rays of the one-dimensional support \(V_{p_\star}\) form the required finite fan; their only proper facet has a nonzero normal on that support.  Equation (27) supplies the zero lower slope and (28) gives \(-D_U\leq0\), so condition (iii) holds even though both LP fibers have multiple optima.  Finally, (12) and \(m_n^2/n\to0\) imply
\[
r_n:=\delta_{m_n}(p_\star)+m_n/\sqrt n+m_n^2/n\longrightarrow0.
\]
The decreasing majorant
\[
\eta_n=\sup_{k\geq n}\sqrt{r_k}
\]
(with an arbitrarily small strictly decreasing perturbation if needed) satisfies \(\eta_n\downarrow0\) and \(r_n/\eta_n\to0\).  Thus (24)--(28) give the exact unit atom at zero and verify every condition of the conservative atomic-tie conclusion on the stated thirty-two-type boundary law.

sampling_model.design: Each unit is assigned independently to a trialed policy \(D\in J_0\) with known probability \(\rho_j>0\); the untrialed policy \(e\) is never assigned.
sampling_model.units: The observed records \(O_i=(D_i,S_i,A_i,Y_i,Z_{\mathrm{obs},i})\) are independent draws from a finite population law induced by one common response-type mixture \(w\in\Delta_{\mathrm{SLCC}}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is the randomized policy index. Policy \(j\) supplies the known recommendation--performance configuration \(c_j(S)\), which elicits action \(A_{c_j(S)}\) and downstream outcome \(Y_{c_j(S)}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every trialed arm has known strictly positive probability \(\rho_j\). No overlap is imposed for \(e\), because its mean is partially identified through structural response restrictions rather than observed assignments.
sampling_model.label_observation: Ground truth \(Z\) is recorded exactly when the endogenous action has \(A=1\); otherwise the recorded label is \(\star\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The only estimated nuisance is the finite multinomial observable law \(p\). Certified performance values and policy configuration maps are treated as external design inputs.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.1 gives valid conditional-mean bounds under counterfactual correctness, performance order, neutrality, and bounded outcomes, while the Tightness of Bounds discussion expressly does not claim those bounds are tight and Appendix G treats only a restricted missing-label mechanism.

Theorems 3.1--3.2 give attained tight bounds for an untrialed model when responses depend on prediction and performance but do not impose counterfactual correctness or action-dependent truth revelation.
Proposition 4.1 bounds contraction error when labels are observed only after a favorable human decision and subjects are randomly assigned across heterogeneous decision makers.
Theorem 3 and Theorem S3 give sharp bounds for AI-alone versus human-system classification risks under a randomized single-blinded evaluation design.

Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 reduce discrete causal models to finite response functions and sharp optimization, while Section 6 and Appendix E propagate simultaneous observable-law confidence regions through those programs.
Calibrated projection yields uniformly asymptotically valid confidence intervals for scalar projections in moment equality and inequality models.
The directional delta method gives non-Gaussian limits for Hadamard directionally differentiable maps, and convex-set projection has tangent-cone projection as its derivative.

Direct bootstrap and \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap constructions for confidence-interval endpoints can fail in finite samples and uniformly in moment-inequality models; the present match is conditional, pointwise atomic-tie validity under an enumerable finite-fan certificate.

tldr: Repeated trials cannot accompany every updated human--AI policy, and in pretrial applications ground truth is revealed only by an endogenous action. The proposal identifies the exact observable--target image of legal finite response types and makes a complete three-performance, two-arm, thirty-two-type quotient the novelty kernel. Its full twelve-cell laws lie in the relative interior of the actual observable polytope and give \([1/2,3/4]\) versus the label-blind \([1/4,1]\), with a perturbed law giving \([397/800,601/800]\) versus \([99/400,1]\). Continuity yields a relatively open region of two-sided strict refinement. Generic simultaneous multinomial confidence-region propagation supplies a finite-sample implementation corollary. Euclidean projection yields a projection-composed directional limit, while conservative centered \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) quantiles at atomic simultaneous ties remain the first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: ZhangSkalnesChenOberst2026 does not claim tightness under its unit-level restrictions and treats only a restricted missing-label mechanism. DuarteFinkelsteinKnoxMummoloShpitser2024 supplies generic finite response-function optimization and confidence-region propagation, but not the legal action-dependent selective-label quotient or a strict full-versus-blind region.
project_justification.niche: A three-performance design makes the trialed low and high configurations bracket an untrialed middle configuration in opposite directions according to latent correctness, so selective revelation of truth can have a stable two-sided identifying value.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the exact finite-response converse, exhausts the full model by thirty-two legal observable--target representatives, verifies a strictly positive full-polytope mixture with exact endpoint arithmetic, derives the relative-open two-sided refinement, and separates generic finite-sample propagation from the new boundary limit and atomic-quantile question.

related_work: Zhang, Skalnes, Chen, and Oberst (2026, Assumptions 3.1--3.3, Theorem 4.1, the Tightness of Bounds discussion, Theorem 5.1, and Appendix G) supply the correctness, performance-order, and neutral restrictions, but do not claim their main bounds are tight and do not treat the present endogenous reveal action. Chen and Oberst (2025, Theorems 3.1--3.2) prove attained bounds in the preceding performance-mediated model without the selective-label correctness quotient. Lakkaraju et al. (2017, p. 4, Proposition 4.1) formalize decision-induced labels through contraction across decision makers rather than a sharp compatible-SCM fiber. Imai et al. (2023) supply the randomized PSA consumer, while Ben-Michael et al. (2025, Theorem 3 and Theorem S3) analyze classification-risk contrasts under a different baseline-potential-outcome design. Duarte et al. (2024, Proposition 1 and Theorem 1) provide the general finite response-function optimization framework, and Section 6 with Appendix E already provides generic propagation of simultaneous observable-law confidence regions; the finite-sample SLCC result is therefore an application corollary. The new theorem-level object is the exhaustive legal thirty-two-type quotient and its relatively open two-sided full-versus-blind refinement. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) provide the calibrated-projection benchmark. Fang and Santos (2019, Theorem 2.1 and Section 4) provide the directional delta method and convex-projection derivative, while the paired LP optimal-face composition is specialized here. Hong and Li (2018) provide a numerical derivative alternative. Andrews and Han (2009) show why centered endpoint subsampling is not justified solely by \(m/n\to0\), motivating the atomic-quantile open question.
technical_internal_limitation: The full-model certificate includes legal realization and actual relative interior. The remaining internal bottleneck is inference at an observable-law projection face when both LPs have multiple optimal bases and the joint directional limit has atoms; weak conditional convergence alone need not validate the required quantile.
honest_scope: The identification results concern finite strata and policies, three distinct certified performance levels in the strictness certificate, and binary actions, labels, and outcomes. Certified performance values are external inputs. Generic confidence-region propagation is used as an implementation result. The projection-composed limit is pointwise, and atomic tie-inclusive subsampling validity is open. Equality of the untrialed and a trialed configuration recovers the randomized observed mean. Full revelation of \(Z\) removes masking but does not identify a distinct untrialed configuration. Multiclass actions, dynamic policies, violation budgets, joint deployment targets, and policy learning remain outside this kernel.
